title: Sentiment
subtitle: Type a company to get a read

bigPicture.lead: Funding AI is the story across big tech this week.
body: Each read covers the last 3 to 5 days and starts from whatever moved the stock: earnings, an equity raise, a regulatory step, or a deal debate.
This week the market rewarded companies that fund AI from their own cash (Microsoft) and punished cash burn or new equity (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta).

driver.title: Search growth slowed to 12% as AI Mode earns less per query

tickers.verdict: Bearish: Search revenue growth slowed sharply and the market repriced Search, even with Cloud doubling.
tickers.topTheme: Search slowing, AI Mode monetizes less
tickers.changed: Reframed around the real driver: the Search growth slowdown. Move confirmed at about 12.6% on Oct 29.

overview.lean: Bearish near term, constructive on 12 months among the Street.

camps.name: Search bears
camps.argues: AI Mode answers more questions but carries fewer ads, so Search growth falling from 17% to 12% is structural, not a blip.

camps.name: Long-term bulls
camps.argues: AI Mode queries are longer and Cloud grew over 100%, so monetization catches up and the selloff overshoots.

overview.agree: Nearly everyone agrees the problem is Search monetization, not Cloud. Cloud more than doubled.
overview.split: Split on whether lower revenue per search is temporary (ads still being added inside AI Mode) or permanent.

shift.note: After the close, the headline miss and negative free cash flow drew immediate selling.
Down about 13% intraday, on track for its worst post-earnings day on record. The Search slowdown became the single story.
Bull rebuttals and dip buying appear, but the high-reach framing is still Search repricing.

overview.hinges: Whether Google can put enough ads into AI Mode to lift revenue per query back up.

tickers.whatHappened: Alphabet reported Q3 on Oct 28. Search revenue grew 12% to $63.35B (Oct 28), down from 17% in Q2, while Cloud grew 103% to $30.7B (Oct 28) and free cash flow was negative $9.07B (Oct 28). Management said AI Mode queries carry lower monetization. The stock fell about 12.6% on Oct 29, its worst post-earnings day on record, erasing roughly $500B of value.
tickers.howReading: Credible voices read it as a repricing of Search economics rather than a rejection of Google's AI position: more questions, less money per question. A minority, including former fund manager Rahul Sharma, point out paid clicks still grew 8% and cost per click 4%, so the slowdown is fewer monetized clicks, not price. The Street mostly cut targets but kept ratings.

driver.title: Azure grew 48% and was guided to 49% to 50%, while staying cash positive

tickers.move: +4% after hours Oct 28, roughly flat Oct 29

camps.argues: Azure accelerated to 48% with a 49% to 50% guide and positive free cash flow, unlike peers.

camps.name: Timing skeptics
camps.argues: Lower capex reflects late third-party capacity, not discipline, so spend catches up later.

overview.agree: Agree Microsoft had the best AI funding story of the week.
overview.split: Split on whether the capex trim is real or just delayed.

shift.note: Up about 4% after hours on the beat and Azure guide.
Gains faded to roughly flat as the Alphabet selloff hit the group.

overview.hinges: Whether supply comes online fast enough to keep Azure near 50% without breaking free cash flow.

tickers.whatHappened: Microsoft reported fiscal Q1 on Oct 28. Revenue was $92.3B vs $90.7B expected (Oct 28) and Azure grew 48% to $33.2B (Oct 28), with next quarter guided to 49% to 50% against about 44.6% expected. Capex of $45.2B came in under estimates and calendar 2026 capex was trimmed to about $170B because third-party capacity arrived late. Free cash flow fell 27% but stayed positive at $18.6B.
tickers.howReading: High-signal accounts framed Microsoft as the self-funding AI winner against Alphabet, Meta and Amazon, which all burned cash. The CFO's line that demand still exceeds supply got the most pickup. The main reservation is that lower capex is timing rather than discipline.

driver.title: Up to $97.5B equity raise with nonvoting Class C shares, offset by Muse momentum

tickers.move: About -2% Oct 26, about -1% Oct 27, -1.2% to -1.4% Oct 29
tickers.verdict: Mixed: a record equity raise and dilution weigh on the stock, offset by Muse momentum and Nvidia buying in.
tickers.topTheme: Equity raise and Class C vs Muse momentum
tickers.changed: Driver changed from Q3 earnings to the Oct 26 equity raise, with Muse momentum as the offset.

camps.name: Dilution and governance bears
camps.argues: Up to $97.5B of stock, nonvoting Class C shares and a pension fund lawsuit mean shareholders fund AI while Zuckerberg keeps control.

camps.name: Muse bulls
camps.argues: Muse is one of the fastest-growing consumer AI apps and Nvidia and AMD are investing $4B alongside, so the spend has a product.

overview.agree: Agree the raise is about funding AI capex after free cash flow turned negative.
overview.split: Split on whether Muse engagement is durable; one Sensor Tower based post says most users stopped returning after two weeks (low reach, unverified).

shift.note: Raise announced: $35B underwritten plus a $60B Class C at-the-market program. Stock down nearly 2%.
Upsized to $25B common at $625 plus $12.5B preferred. Nvidia commits $3B and expands the Muse partnership. Pension fund sues over the restructuring.
Offerings close; stock down about 1.2% on dilution worries.

overview.hinges: Whether Muse and AI revenue grow fast enough to justify roughly 5% to 6% dilution and the credit-market stress.

tickers.whatHappened: On Oct 26 Meta launched its largest-ever equity raise: $25B of Class A common priced at $625 via forward sales (no upfront cash, settles by Nov 19, 2027), $12.5B of 6.50% mandatory convertible preferred, and a planned $60B at-the-market program in new nonvoting Class C shares starting in Q1 2027. On Oct 27 Nvidia committed $3B and AMD $1B, and Nvidia expanded its partnership on Muse, Meta's AI agent. This followed Q3 results on Oct 21 with negative free cash flow of $2.12B and record 5-year CDS spreads.
tickers.howReading: Credible voices read it as Meta funding AI with shareholders' money while protecting Zuckerberg's control, which is why Barron's and a pension fund lawsuit focused on the Class C structure. Analysts estimate full execution could dilute holders by about 5% to 6% (Investing.com, Oct 29). The offset is Muse: Nvidia's investment and the expanded partnership are read as validation of demand. The credit angle (record CDS after Q3) keeps the debate in the bond market too.

driver.title: Third quarter beat, but a fourth quarter guide far below the Street on a sharp PC slowdown

tickers.move: Down about 25% to 29% intraday on October 30 (around $66), after closing near $92 on October 29; on track for its worst day on record
tickers.verdict: Bearish: the PC reset and a cash-burning 2027 overwhelm a strong server quarter, and the Street is cutting targets across the board.
tickers.topTheme: PC collapse swamps the server CPU boom
tickers.changed: New read. First time Intel is tracked.

overview.lean: Bearish near term. Even the bulls concede the guide was a reset; the debate is whether the long-term foundry and server thesis survives it.

camps.name: Reset bears (most of the sell side)
camps.argues: The PC business hit a wall, Intel did not see it coming, its factories are still sized for PCs rather than servers, and 2027 is a heavy capex year with free cash flow probably not positive. BofA downgraded to neutral; Bernstein, UBS, Wells Fargo and Barclays cut targets to $75 to $80.

camps.name: Long-term bulls
camps.argues: Server CPU demand is extraordinary (Intel sees server CPU TAM growing up to 5x over five years, units up 30%+ in 2026 and 2027), data center grew 78%, and the foundry story did not change. Patrick Moorhead said the reaction does not make sense.

overview.agree: Agree the third quarter itself was good and that server demand is real but supply constrained (substrates, the Israel fab outage). Agree the PC slump runs at least through the first half of 2027 with no memory price relief.
overview.split: Split on whether a demand boom Intel cannot fully supply is a temporary bottleneck or proof it is losing the CPU cycle to AMD and TSMC.

shift.note: Intel announces the Classiq quantum software deal; read as a sign of balance sheet confidence. Stock near its best year on record.
Before the report the stock slips about 3.6%. After the bell, the Q4 guide of $15B to $16B against about $17B expected sends shares down more than 20% after hours.
Wave of target cuts and a BofA downgrade. Shares fall as much as 29%, and Intel's 5-year credit default swap widens to a record.

overview.hinges: Whether server supply (substrates, the Israel fab, shifting Oregon capacity to Intel 3) ramps through 2027 fast enough to offset PCs, and whether Intel names the external packaging and foundry customers it teased for the next two quarters.

tickers.whatHappened: On October 29 after the close, Intel reported third quarter revenue of $16.5B, up 21%, and adjusted EPS of $0.52 against $0.40 expected. Data center and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3B, while client computing fell 5% to $8.1B. The fourth quarter guide was $15B to $16B in revenue and $0.25 adjusted EPS, against roughly $17B and $0.43 expected (LSEG). Management said the PC correction accelerated over the last two months, expects client revenue down more than 20% sequentially, sees the PC slowdown lasting at least through the first half of 2027, and said Intel does not expect positive cash flow this year. The October explosion at its Israel fab is expected to cost roughly $600M of revenue over two quarters (Reuters). On October 30 the stock fell as much as 29%, its sharpest one-day drop on record.
tickers.howReading: The sell side read it as a reset, not a blip. BofA's Vivek Arya downgraded to neutral and cut his target to $100 from $145, citing too little external foundry traction and a sharp PC drop. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon cut to $75 from $110, modeling data center well above the Street but client far below it, with Intel shifting some Oregon capacity from PCs to server chips. UBS, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Goldman framed it as a PC hole that swallows the server upside. Industry analyst Patrick Moorhead is the main credible pushback: he called the quarter good, said the selloff does not make sense for a multiyear foundry thesis, and pointed to AMD's report next week as the test of whether the supply pain is Intel specific. The biggest reach on X was headline traffic (Walter Bloomberg, StockMKTNewz, Investing.com) on the record drop and record-wide credit spreads.

facts.label: Stock move

tickers.controversy: Whether this is a supply problem or a demand problem. Bulls say demand is strong and Intel simply cannot ship enough server chips; bears say the PC wall plus capacity in the wrong places shows the turnaround is slipping. AMD's report next week is the widely cited test of whether the PC and substrate pain is Intel specific.

method: Each read looks back about 3 to 5 days and names the real driver of the stock move. Posts come from X public search by cashtag and company name, filtered to credible voices (sell-side and buy-side analysts, fund managers, respected investors, financial journalists, company executives) and ranked by views, then likes. Memes, hype and recap bots are dropped. Post dates and counts come from X and were captured Oct 30, 2026. Moves and analyst targets come from free news sources. Anything marked unverified could not be confirmed.
